title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: On three hourly load datasets (ISO-NE, CAISO and an anonymous utility), Chronos-2 is the most accurate of four foundation models and four trained-from-scratch models when future covariates are exact or mildly noisy, but TimesNet is more robust once the covariate forecasts become very noisy.
why_relevant: Hourly ISO load with weather covariates and a test of degraded covariate forecasts, which is close to our oracle versus forecast regimes.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: EnergyBench / Foretec Energy Bench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: In the first 32 live days, adding the same frozen weather covariates cut the error of ten foundation models by 37-51% in matched comparisons, zero-shot models matched a LightGBM on the same covariates, and for load the best models trailed the grid operators' own forecasts by 4-6%.
why_relevant: A live (not backtested) energy benchmark that runs foundation models with and without identical weather inputs, including load, but at day-ahead and for European zones.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: Zero-shot Chronos-2 is clearly worse than task-specific deep models on ISO New England and ENTSO-E zonal load, and only after fine-tuning does it win at short horizons, with its error growing faster as the horizon lengthens.
why_relevant: Zonal ISO-NE load with weather and calendar covariates and a finding that zero-shot accuracy degrades with horizon, which bears directly on our week-ahead primary comparison (daily data, so the horizon does not match).

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Pretrained foundation models beat seasonal-naive and XGBoost baselines at four load aggregation levels, and rank-16 LoRA on MOIRAI 1.0 Large lowers normalized MAE by about 7.5% on average, with Chronos-2 used to check transfer.
why_relevant: Compares pretrained inference with adaptation for electrical load across aggregation levels, although the horizon and covariates are not stated in the abstract.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (t0-alpha, t0-beta)
claim: Open-weights 102M and 256M models take past and known-future covariates without retraining, rank third on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, and raise skill by about 6 points on tasks with known-future covariates.
why_relevant: A runnable open model with native known-future covariates; the paper also cites a Victoria electricity-demand benchmark.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models (5M to 209M)
claim: Four CPU-friendly zero-shot models with native known-future covariate support, where the 209M model is reported by Mistral to lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench and the 28M model to beat Chronos-2.
why_relevant: Already on our runnable list (Timestral-209M); the release date and weights commit decide its weeks-after-weights label for our scored window.

title: TimesFM-3: natively multivariate zero-shot forecasting with covariates
claim: A 330M model that takes multiple targets plus past-only and known-future covariates in one pass and is reported by Google to rank first among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME; the weights are non-commercial.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable runnable model (weather as a known-future input); the licence is non-commercial.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: Chronos-2 gives the lowest error in high-demand periods at area, substation and feeder level on UK and Swiss open data, ahead of LightGBM, XGBoost, statistical baselines and Chronos-Bolt.
why_relevant: Compares Chronos-2 with gradient-boosted regressors on load, but at distribution level and short horizons.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: An adaptive GAM with state-space updating that aggregates several weather forecast providers improves point and probabilistic load forecasts by diluting the effect of weather prediction errors.
why_relevant: Directly about using archived weather forecasts (not actuals) as load covariates, matching our forecast regime; no foundation model involved.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building, TimesFM 3.0 with covariates cuts MAE by about 43% against weekly seasonal naive, but paired daily tests show no clear advantage over XGBoost, and weather covariates use retrospective observations.
why_relevant: Compares TimesFM 3.0 with covariates against XGBoost on the same inputs, but for one building, day-ahead, with observed weather.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act requirements: results from a 41-day live challenge on German transmission-grid load
claim: In a 41-day live challenge on German TSO load, a deterministic open-source pipeline with calendar and weather covariates beat the ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast, and small local models were competitive with Chronos-2.
why_relevant: A live load challenge with a foundation-model comparison, but only 41 days (under our 90-day minimum) and a day-ahead horizon.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Choosing Load Forecasting Methods by Horizon, History and Hour: Reserve and Imbalance Evidence from Four Grids (companion data and code)
claim: A reproduction package with a pre-specified protocol and a log of deviations compares rolling-origin load forecasts at horizons of 1 to 180 days and hourly day-ahead forecasts on four national grids, with online selection and conformal intervals.
why_relevant: Has a pre-specified protocol with deviations logged and covers horizons that include a week, but the record does not say which models or covariates were used (not confirmed beyond the record text).
query: site:zenodo.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactual truth, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 answer what-if covariate queries with the observational slope and respond more strongly than a regression does.
why_relevant: Preregistered evidence on how covariate-aware foundation models use a covariate such as temperature, though on synthetic data and not on load.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models
claim: Chronos-2, t0-beta and TiRex-2 respond more strongly to a covariate supplied as several identical channels, and in a public energy dataset a duplicated weather station changes day-ahead forecasts; declaring the source removes the effect.
why_relevant: Bears on how temperature must be supplied to covariate models so every model sees the identical series (our rule 3).
query: site:zenodo.org TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: A timestamped preregistration compares Timestral-5M and 209M and Chronos-2 (no covariates) with SARIMA and GBM baselines on hourly 96-hour carbon intensity, with all three models ahead by roughly 1 MAPE point on a 2025 test and contamination not ruled out.
why_relevant: A preregistered hourly multi-day backtest with a Timestral and Chronos-2 comparison, but the target is carbon intensity and there are no covariates.
query: site:arxiv.org zero-shot forecasting with covariates weather

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: A new tabular foundation model release that reports stronger time-series forecasting through its task harness and adds faster and thinking variants; weights are under a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: TabPFN-TS accepts known-future covariates such as weather forecasts, but the report's forecasting results are not specific to load.
query: site:github.com zero-shot forecasting with covariates weather

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: A tabular foundation model with economic indicators forecasts French load 1 to 48 months ahead at monthly and daily resolution, and economic data narrows the gap to long-term methods.
why_relevant: Electricity load with a foundation model, but at monthly and daily resolution and far beyond a week.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark on ESHED-38
claim: On 48 weekly origins over a 359-day holdout for 38 homes, Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot model one day ahead and ties TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-Bolt at one week, with the best configurations about 20-25% better than seasonal naive.
why_relevant: Weekly rolling origins and a one-week lead time with Chronos-2, but daily smart-meter data for homes in Iraq.
query: site:arxiv.org pre-registered forecasting backtest energy demand
